_doc: Shared ECalc vectors. The Go tests (internal/ecalc) and the JavaScript parity test run the same file.
A numeric want is a JSON number or one of the strings "nan", "inf", "-inf".
Numbers match when the relative error is at most 1e-12; a zero want allows an absolute error of 1e-12.
Keys starting with _doc are documentation. Every other top-level key is a list of vectors.
_doc_expr: expr: parse src, evaluate it with env (name -> number) and lists (name -> array of numbers); the result must equal want.
_doc_eval_error: eval_error: src parses, but evaluating it with env and lists must fail (unknown identifier, list outside sum/par, sum/par argument that is not a list).
_doc_parse: parse: ParseExpr(src) must succeed and print as ast. Prefix notation: (op l r) for binary operators, (neg a), (pos a), (fn arg ...) for calls, numbers exactly as written, identifiers by name. Parentheses leave no node.
_doc_formula: formula: ParseFormula(src) must succeed and print as ast. The top node is (= part part ...), also for a formula without '='.
_doc_deps: deps: the sorted unique identifiers of ParseExpr(src), without function names and without pi.

deps.src: lookup_ge(t, c, a+b, out) * interp(t, p, q, z)

_doc_round_sig: round_sig: round x to n significant digits and return the nearest double of that decimal. Exact decimal ties round away from zero (the behaviour of JavaScript's Number(x.toPrecision(n))); the comparison is exact.
_doc_eseries: eseries: Nearest(series, v) returns the standard value want (relative deviation, a tie goes to the lower value) and dev = (want - v) / v * 100.
_doc_eseries_error: eseries_error: Nearest(series, v) must fail (unknown series, v not finite, not greater than zero, or below the smallest normal double 2.2250738585072014e-308: the logarithm of a denormal is not reliable).
_doc_combine: combine: Combine(series, target, limit) returns want. The first entry is the single nearest standard value (kind single, r2 0); then up to limit series pairs (r1 >= r2, value r1 + r2, both values in [target/1000, target]) and up to limit parallel pairs (r1 <= r2, value r1*r2/(r1+r2), both values in [target, 1000*target]). Candidates are mantissa x 10^k rounded to 3 significant digits. Each group is ordered by the absolute deviation (deviations that are equal within 1e-9 percent are ties), then r1, then r2 ascending. dev_pct = (value - target) / target * 100; r1, r2 and value match at 1e-12 relative, dev_pct at 1e-9 (absolute 1e-12 when the expected deviation is 0). The order of the entries must match exactly.

combine.ref: hand: 4.7k is 6% below 5k and 5.6k 12% above, so the single is 4.7k; best series 4.7k+270 = 4970 (-0.6%) and 4.7k+330 = 5030 (+0.6%) tie on |deviation|, R2 ascending; 10k || 10k = 5k exactly
hand: 1k is an E24 value (single, deviation 0); 820+180 = 1000, 910+91 = 1001, 1k+1 = 1001; 1.1k || 11k, 1.5k || 3k and 2k || 2k are exactly 1k and are ordered by R1
hand: 4.75k is an E96 value (single, deviation 0); 2.43k+2.32k, 2.49k+2.26k and 3.01k+1.74k are exactly 4.75k
hand: the target is a decade boundary: series candidates run from 0.001 to 1 (1+0.001 = 1.001, +0.1%), parallel candidates from 1 to 1000 (1 || 1000 = 0.999)
hand: 0.27+0.2 is 0.47000000000000003 in doubles (deviation 1e-14 percent) and ties with the exact 0.36+0.11: deviations equal within 1e-9 percent are ties, so R1 ascending puts 0.27 first
hand: the neighbours of 333.3 are 332 (-0.39%) and 336; 2.61+72.3 and 2.84+49.3 are exactly 333.3
hand: a limit of 0 leaves only the single entry

hand: 1e306 is an E24 value (single, deviation 0); target*1000 overflows to +Inf, so the parallel group has no range and is skipped; 8.2e305+1.8e305 = 1e306 exactly, 9.1e305+9.1e304 and 1e306+1e303 are +0.1%, then 1e306+1.1e303 (+0.11%) and 1e306+1.2e303 (+0.12%)

hand: 1.8e305 is an E24 value (single, deviation 0); 1000*target is above the largest double, so the parallel group is skipped; 1.5e305+3e304 and 1.6e305+2e304 are exactly 1.8e305, then 1.8e305 plus 1.8e302, 2e302 and 2.2e302 (+0.1%, +0.1111%, +0.1222%)

_doc_combine_count: combine_count: Combine(series, target, limit) returns exactly want entries: 1 + the series pairs + the parallel pairs, each group capped at min(limit, 1000). E3 has 10 values in each of the two three-decade ranges around 100, so 10*11/2 = 55 pairs per group; E96 around 5000 has more than 1000 pairs per group, so a huge limit is capped.
_doc_combine_error: combine_error: Combine(series, target, 5) must fail (unknown series, target not finite, not greater than zero, or a denormal: below 2.2250738585072014e-308, like eseries_error). A group whose range bound is 0, a denormal or +Inf (target/1000 or target*1000 outside the doubles) has no range and is skipped, see the 1e306 and 1.8e305 cases of combine.
_doc_units_parse: units_parse: Parse(in, dim, unit) returns want in the SI base unit. unit is the selected explicit unit id (absent or empty = none). A value is 0 or has a magnitude within 1e-300 .. 1e300 (both ends are valid).
_doc_units_parse_error: units_parse_error: Parse(in, dim, unit) must fail. A result that is not finite (1e400, a prefix that overflows) is an error, and so is a nonzero result (after the unit conversion) whose magnitude is above 1e300 or below 1e-300; 4R7 only reads on a dimension with the alias R (resistance). The text as typed (blanks included) may be at most 64 characters long (UTF-16 code units).
_doc_units_list: units_list: ParseList(in, dim, unit) splits on semicolons, white space and commas that are not followed by a digit (a comma before a digit is a decimal comma, so 4,7k, 10k is two items and 1,2,3 is one unreadable item), parses every item like Parse and skips empty items. Text longer than 256 characters, or an item longer than 64, is an error (see units_parse_error).
_doc_units_format: units_format: Format(v, dim, unit, sig) returns want. v is a number or "nan"/"inf"/"-inf" (result ""); unit is the selected explicit unit id (absent = automatic prefix); sig defaults to 4.
_doc_units_roundtrip: units_roundtrip: Format(v, dim, unit) must equal text, text must be at most 64 characters long (the longest text Parse accepts) and Parse(text, dim, unit) must give v again. The largest value 9007199254740991 is 61 characters in binary because binary groups by eight digits (hex groups by four, which is 19 characters).
_doc_solve_range: solve_range: a primary variable of dimension dim (any input, no rules) that Solve receives with the SI value v gets the error code want ("" = none). nan and inf are "nonfinite"; zero or less is "range" for a positive dimension; a value that is not an integer in 0 .. 9007199254740991 is "range" for a dimension with integer: true.
_doc_table_fixture: table_fixture: the catalog of the table vectors below. files are the YAML files of a catalog tree (a line list per file; NAME16 stands for a name written in all 16 locales); items are what the catalog JSON (LocalizedJSON en) carries for them. The Go tests check that the items are exactly what Load and LocalizedJSON make of the files, the JavaScript test registers the items with ECalcCore.tables, so both sides evaluate the same tables.

_doc_table_functions: table_functions: parse expr, evaluate it with env (name -> number) and refs (table alias -> table or column id, the aliases a selected choice option defines) against the tables of table_fixture; the result must equal want (a number, or "nan" for no result). lookup(T, C, key) is the value of column C in the row whose key column equals key (within 1e-9 relative); lookup_ge(T, C, x, OUT) is column OUT of the first row whose column C is filled and at least x; interp(T, X, Y, x) is the linear interpolation of Y over X through the rows where both are filled, exact at the nodes and NaN outside the range of X. Every want is worked out from the rows of the table named in ref.

_doc_table_function_errors: table_function_errors: expr parses, but evaluating it with env and refs against the tables of table_fixture must fail: an unknown table or column, a text column, a text key column for lookup, an alias that is not defined, an unknown variable.

table_function_errors.ref: the output column n is text
t_txt has a text key column, lookup needs a numeric key
the alias tbl is not defined, so tbl is taken as a table id and there is none
an unknown variable in the key
an alias that points to no table

_doc_table_solve: table_solve: Solve of the calculator ec_fix of table_fixture (variable q, choices src: a|b selects the table t_fix|t_alt and col: y|z the column, rules r = lookup, derived s = lookup_ge and i = interp) from the SI inputs with the choices; expect lists values ("nan" for NaN), errors is the exact error map.

table_solve.ref: defaults a/y, q = 2: r = y at x = 2; s = x of the first z >= 2 (x = 1); i = z at x = 2
t_fix, column z, q = 4: r = z at x = 4 = 400; s = x of the first z >= 4 (x = 1); i = z at x = 4
t_fix, q = 3: no row has x = 3, so r is NaN (nonfinite); s = 1; i = halfway between 200 and 400
t_fix, q = 0.5: below the first node, so r and i are NaN; s = 1
t_alt, column y, q = 20: r = 2.5; s = x of the first z >= 20 (z = 25, x = 30); i = z at x = 20 = 15
t_alt, q = 25: no row has x = 25, so r is NaN; s = 30 (z = 25 is at least 25); i = halfway between 15 and 25

_doc_eseries_tables: eseries_tables: the mantissas of one decade (1 <= m < 10) of every series, as listed by IEC 60063. The JavaScript mirror must carry exactly these tables (E192 has 9.20 at index 185).
